stem: 7. Let A and B be two overlapping sets and the universal set be U. Draw appropriate Venn diagram for each of the following,

entries.question: (i) A∪B
steps: Begin with a universal rectangle U containing two overlapping circles labelled A and B. The four distinct regions are A-only, A∩B, B-only and outside both.
Shade every point in A or B, including the overlap.
The selected region(s) are: A-only, A∩B, and B-only.
Check each of the four regions using whether its points belong to A and B. All of A and all of B.
entries.answer: All of A and all of B

entries.question: (ii) A∩B
steps: Begin with a universal rectangle U containing two overlapping circles labelled A and B. The four distinct regions are A-only, A∩B, B-only and outside both.
Shade only points that belong to both A and B.
The selected region(s) are: A∩B.
Check each of the four regions using whether its points belong to A and B. Only the overlapping region.

entries.question: (iii) (A∩B)′
steps: Begin with a universal rectangle U containing two overlapping circles labelled A and B. The four distinct regions are A-only, A∩B, B-only and outside both.
First identify the overlap A∩B, then take its complement relative to U.
The selected region(s) are: A-only, B-only, outside both.
Check each of the four regions using whether its points belong to A and B. Everywhere in U except the overlap.
entries.answer: Everywhere in U except the overlap

entries.question: (iv) (B–A)′
steps: Begin with a universal rectangle U containing two overlapping circles labelled A and B. The four distinct regions are A-only, A∩B, B-only and outside both.
First identify B–A: the part of B that is outside A. Shade its complement in U.
The selected region(s) are: A-only, A∩B, outside both.
Check each of the four regions using whether its points belong to A and B. Everywhere in U except the B-only region.
entries.answer: Everywhere in U except the B-only region

entries.question: (v) A′∪B′
steps: Begin with a universal rectangle U containing two overlapping circles labelled A and B. The four distinct regions are A-only, A∩B, B-only and outside both.
Shade points outside A or outside B; the only excluded points lie in both.
The selected region(s) are: A-only, B-only, outside both.
Check each of the four regions using whether its points belong to A and B. Everywhere in U except the overlap.

entries.question: (vi) A′∩B′
steps: Begin with a universal rectangle U containing two overlapping circles labelled A and B. The four distinct regions are A-only, A∩B, B-only and outside both.
Shade points outside A and outside B simultaneously.
The selected region(s) are: outside both.
Check each of the four regions using whether its points belong to A and B. Only the region outside both sets.

entries.question: (vii) What do you observe from the Venn diagram (iii) and (v)?
steps: Begin with a universal rectangle U containing two overlapping circles labelled A and B. The four distinct regions are A-only, A∩B, B-only and outside both.
Compare the region shaded for (A∩B)′ with the region shaded for A′∪B′.
The selected region(s) are: A-only, B-only, outside both.
Check each of the four regions using whether its points belong to A and B. The shaded regions are identical: (A∩B)′ = A′∪B′..
entries.answer: The shaded regions are identical: (A∩B)′ = A′∪B′.
